solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Delta knocking 20 per cent off drink (8)

indicatorNotes.knocking 20 per cent off: RIVERMOUTH has ten letters, so a fifth of it is two letters, knocked off the front

blocks.note: a delta is where a river meets the sea: a river mouth
RI, two of the ten letters, removed

annotation.surface: An airline passenger notices that Delta has cut the price of drinks by a fifth.
annotation.walkthrough: Delta reads as the airline, or the letter D in the NATO alphabet; it is the mouth of a river, and the percentage is worked out on the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified, flavoured wine drunk as an aperitif.

entries.clue: One seen climbing across building receiving rapier wound (8,7)

indicatorNotes.wound: wound as in twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A climber scaling a building is run through by a rapier and wounded.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wound" reads as an injury from the rapier; it is the past tense of wind. The definition is the long first half: the plant that covers house walls.
annotation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine often grown over the walls of buildings.

entries.clue: Went through again to bowl, having changed ends (7)

indicatorNotes.having changed ends: the first and last letters trade places

blocks.note: in cricket the bowler delivers the ball
D and R swap places

annotation.surface: A cricket bowler repeats an over after the teams switch ends.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowlers really do change ends between overs, so the phrase sits naturally in the surface; here it moves the letters D and R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to live an experience a second time, in memory, is to go through it again.

entries.clue: Signs of Gallic strongman losing vote (5)

indicatorNotes.losing: the vote letter is dropped from the name

blocks.note: Obelix, Asterix's menhir-carrying friend in the French comic
you mark a ballot with an X
OBELIX without X

annotation.surface: A French strongman is shown the signs that he has lost an election.
annotation.walkthrough: An obelus (plural obeli) is the dagger or division sign used in old manuscripts and printing.
annotation.definitionFit: Obeli are the dagger marks or division signs used in texts.

entries.clue: Problem for choppers, heart of wood breaking defective hatchet (9)

indicatorNotes.heart of: the heart is the middle, the two Os of WOOD
indicatorNotes.breaking: the OO breaks into the other letters
indicatorNotes.defective: the hatchet is faulty, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: middle letters of wOOd
anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A woodcutter's broken hatchet causes trouble for anyone doing the chopping.
annotation.walkthrough: "Choppers" is slang for teeth, not axemen, even though the surface is all about cutting wood.
annotation.definitionFit: Toothache is literally a problem for your choppers, meaning your teeth.

entries.clue: Get off sled, perhaps, in downpour (6)

blocks.note: de- is the prefix for removing, as in de-plane
a luge is a racing sled

annotation.surface: A tobogganer is told to climb off the sled when it starts pouring.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is to read DELUGE as a made-up verb, de-luge, meaning to get off a luge, just as deplane means to leave an aircraft.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name rain falling in a flood, and deluge can also stretch to any overwhelming rush.

entries.clue: Quote half-hearted English novelist about having vigour (9)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: GREENE's heart is EE; losing half of it drops one E

blocks.note: to quote a source is to cite it
Graham GREENE with one of the middle Es gone

annotation.surface: A critic quotes a lacklustre English novelist on the subject of vigour.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" looks like "on the subject of", but it reverses CITE plus GRENE together to give ENERGETIC.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective phrase matching an adjective: full of energy and full of vigour describe the same lively person.

entries.clue: Tense? Let go (7)

blocks.note: tense = taut, the opposite of slack; the question mark flags a made-up reading
let go = release, set free

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the first sense as a joke: tense means not loose, so un-loose. The real word means the opposite, to loosen or release.
annotation.definitionFit: To unloose something is to let it go or set it free.

entries.clue: Old love letter perhaps being dismissed by church authorities (15)

blocks.note: ex = former
a love letter is one kind of communication

annotation.surface: A priest's old love letter turns up and he is thrown out by his bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a love letter got a clergyman sacked; "perhaps" marks the love letter as just one example of the wider word.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun phrase for the formal act: the church expels a member, cutting them off from its sacraments.

entries.clue: Employed boss at NYT? (4)

blocks.note: the New York Times is an American paper
the editor, the boss of a newspaper

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a person was hired by the New York Times's boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: the boss at the New York Times is an American editor, US ED.
annotation.definitionFit: Employed and used both mean put to work.

entries.clue: Olivier developed work of some depth (7)

indicatorNotes.developed: developed as in worked into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Laurence Olivier developed a performance with real depth.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Olivier's acting; rilievo is Italian for relief sculpture, carved out from a background to a certain depth.
annotation.definitionFit: Rilievo is relief sculpture, a work standing out to some depth from its ground.

entries.clue: Old record producer’s name recalled by woman (7)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the word runs backwards
indicatorNotes.by: by in its sense of beside, so the reversed name stands next to the woman

blocks.note: she = a woman
to call is to name; CALL reversed

annotation.surface: A woman remembers the name of the man who produced an old record.
annotation.walkthrough: "Record producer" suggests a person in a studio, but it is the material: old 78 rpm records were pressed from shellac.
annotation.definitionFit: Shellac, a resin, was the stuff old gramophone records were made from.

entries.clue: Attack in speech? Did just that (9)

annotation.definition: Attack in speech? Did just that

blocks.note: looks like a question about how to describe an attack; it is a definition of a verb meaning to rail against
asks for that verb in the past tense: someone who has already done it

annotation.walkthrough: The first half defines the verb INVEIGH, and the second asks for the past tense: someone who did just that inveighed.
annotation.definitionFit: To inveigh is to speak out violently against something, so inveighed is attacked in speech.

entries.clue: Man of the match in space on heading in goal (5)

indicatorNotes.heading in: the heading is the first letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down or across clue, on = placed after

blocks.note: first letter of goal
room = space

annotation.surface: A footballer named man of the match heads the ball into space in front of goal.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface misleads: the match is a wedding, and its man is the groom.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by wordplay on match: a marriage is a match, and at a wedding the bridegroom is its man.

entries.clue: List where cards are in report (5)

indicatorNotes.in report: report = something spoken, so we go by sound

blocks.note: playing cards are kept in decks

annotation.surface: Someone asks for a list saying where the cards are, according to a report.
annotation.walkthrough: An index can be a card index, which makes the surface feel like office filing.
annotation.definitionFit: An index is an alphabetical list, as at the back of a book.

entries.clue: Times tips for Brighton and Epsom include rank no-hope outsiders I fear (9)

indicatorNotes.tips for: the tips are the first letters
indicatorNotes.include: X and BE hold the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.rank: rank = foul, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times
NOHOPE rearranged
first letters of Brighton and Epsom

annotation.surface: A newspaper racing tipster at Brighton and Epsom includes some no-hope outsiders, sadly.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing words (tips, rank outsiders, no-hope) all belong to the surface; Brighton and Epsom are English racecourses. The definition is spoken by the xenophobe himself: outsiders I fear.
annotation.definitionFit: A xenophobe is someone who fears or hates foreigners, so outsiders I fear is his motto.

entries.clue: Exercise caution re drink (9)

indicatorNotes.Exercise: to exercise is to work, and the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Advice to go carefully with alcohol.
annotation.walkthrough: "Exercise caution" is a stock phrase, which hides that exercise is the instruction and caution the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a French orange liqueur is one brand of drink.

entries.clue: Messy, I’d clean it all the same (9)

indicatorNotes.Messy: a mess of letters to be tidied into a word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone shrugs that, however messy the thing is, they would clean it anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: "All the same" reads as "nevertheless" in the surface; it is the definition, meaning exactly alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: all the same, read as an adjective phrase, means matching in every detail.

entries.clue: Conservative set defending right to property for patrons (9)

indicatorNotes.defending: the outer letters surround and guard the right

blocks.note: C = Conservative, TELE = a television set
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

annotation.surface: A Conservative group defends property rights on behalf of its patrons.
annotation.walkthrough: "Set" reads as a group of Conservatives, but it is a television set; tele is an old British word for a TV.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun matching a plural: the whole body of a shop's regular customers.

entries.clue: To gratify member of ruling party, expected to embrace flag regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: DUE holds the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other-one rhythm

blocks.note: the party in power is in; its members are the ins
due = expected, as in due at noon
the 2nd and 4th letters of fLaG

annotation.surface: A party loyalist is expected to embrace the flag to please the leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: "Member of ruling party" reads as a whole person, but it gives only two letters: the governing side is in, the opposition out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the infinitive's "to" matched: both mean give someone the pleasure they want.

entries.clue: Sign crop’s failing for island (5)

indicatorNotes.failing: the crop fails, so it vanishes from the sign

blocks.note: a sign of the zodiac
CORN, a crop, is taken away

annotation.surface: A farmer sees a failed harvest as an omen to leave for an island.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's "sign" is an omen, but it is a star sign, and the crop is CORN inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is one particular island, off the coast near Naples.

entries.clue: I study South American nation’s former queen (7)

blocks.note: Peru
the possessive S
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth

annotation.surface: A historian studies a former queen of a South American country.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: a peruser is someone who can say "I study". ER is now a former queen because Elizabeth II has died.
annotation.definitionFit: A peruser reads or studies something carefully, so "I study" is what one would say.

entries.clue: Finally find oneself back in the saddle (3,2)

blocks.note: the back end of something
a jockey who is riding is up

annotation.surface: A rider eventually finds themself back on the horse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Back in the saddle" is a set phrase for returning to work, so it hides that the two halves work separately; racing reports say a jockey is up when riding.
annotation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to finally find yourself there.

entries.clue: Suffering clergyman and agents scratching heads — what’s causing rash? (9)

indicatorNotes.scratching heads: each word's head, its first letter, is scratched out

blocks.note: HURT without its H
VICAR without its V
CIA, the American spy agency, without its C

annotation.surface: A vicar and some agents are scratching their heads over what has brought on a skin complaint.
annotation.walkthrough: "Scratching heads" suggests puzzled people, and also itching; it takes the first letter off all three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Urticaria is hives, an itchy skin rash.

entries.clue: Ready for university, turn over a new leaf (2,2)

blocks.note: U = university
PTO, please turn over, is written at the foot of a page to send you to the next leaf

annotation.surface: A student ready for university resolves to make a fresh start.
annotation.walkthrough: "Turn over a new leaf" is an idiom for reforming; here it is literal, turning a page, which is what PTO asks.
annotation.definitionFit: Up to a task means ready for it or capable of it.

entries.clue: Bellyache about cops removing clothing (5)

indicatorNotes.removing clothing: the clothing is the outside, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: c = circa, about
POLICE without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone complains about police officers stripping off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bellyache" reads as a verb, to complain; it is the noun, a pain in the belly.
annotation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, a bellyache.

entries.clue: Withdrawal — drink not an option (4-3)

blocks.note: a pull is a swig from a bottle or glass
an idea that is out is ruled out

annotation.surface: Someone in withdrawal is told that drinking is no longer an option.
annotation.walkthrough: "Withdrawal" reads as a recovering drinker's symptoms; it is the military sense, an army leaving.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the military sense: troops leaving a region.

entries.clue: Company beginning to implode after mislaying substantial figures (7)

indicatorNotes.after: after in its sense of following in sequence, so the I is placed behind LOSS

blocks.note: Co. = company
mislaying something is a loss
first letter of implode

annotation.surface: A company starts to collapse after losing substantial sums.
annotation.walkthrough: The business surface makes "figures" look like money; they are giant statues, like the Colossus of Rhodes.
annotation.definitionFit: Colossi are huge statues, very substantial figures.

entries.clue: Colour associated with sea in which fish swam (6)

indicatorNotes.in which: the fish goes in the colour

blocks.note: the Red Sea
an eel is a fish

annotation.surface: A painter chooses a sea colour in which fish are swimming.
annotation.walkthrough: "Swam" belongs to the fish in the surface; it means a head that swam, dizzy, i.e. reeled.
annotation.definitionFit: When your head swims or reels, you feel giddy.

entries.clue: Put Reagan in power? It’s a little bit charged (8)

blocks.note: put … in power = voted into office; the phrase is split around Reagan
the second half of put in power, carrying no letters of its own
Ronald Reagan, US president, was Ron

annotation.surface: Voting Ronald Reagan into office was, as it turned out, somewhat controversial.
annotation.walkthrough: "Charged" suggests a politically charged decision; the definition means a tiny particle carrying an electric charge.
annotation.definitionFit: An electron is a tiny subatomic particle with a negative charge.
